rhs.name: Rosa The Generous Gardener ('Ausdrawn') (Cl)
rhs.note: 'The Generous Gardener' is a trade designation; the cultivar epithet is 'Ausdrawn'.

palette.role: Repeat pink flowers and scent at low to middle height.

attachment.supportNeeds: Open frame with strong, discreet tie points and access for cutting; thorn-safe clearance from visitors.

wood.basis: BBC Gardeners' World Magazine: "Climbing roses flower on growth produced in the current year", unlike ramblers, which flower on the previous year's growth. A statement about climbing roses as a class (RHS pruning group 17), not about this cultivar. The flowering shoots are side shoots from the tied-in framework of older canes, which is why the RHS shortens flowered side shoots in winter and keeps the framework.

monthsUK.basis: Months read from the RHS season wording (spring = Mar-May, summer = Jun-Aug, autumn = Sep-Nov, winter = Dec-Feb; early, mid and late are the first, second and third month).

flowering.display: Strongly scented semi-double pale-pink flowers, repeat-flowering.

site.aspect: Full sun or partial shade; flowers best where light reaches the cane framework.

calendar.note: RHS pruning group 17: routine pruning between December and February, after the flowers have faded. Remove dead, diseased or dying wood, then cut flowered side shoots back by two thirds; where congested, cut out an old cane at the base.
RHS: in autumn tie in or shorten long whippy shoots before winter winds; at the winter prune tie in the new shoots needed to fill the support.
RHS: deadhead during the flowering season to encourage repeat flowering. Months are the flowering envelope above.
RHS rose guide: feed in March or April before flowering and again in midsummer after the first flush, then mulch.

management.notes: Every attachment is a gardener tie. Tie in new canes, prune, renew old canes, deadhead where wanted; inspect where thorns meet the public. The RHS describes it as growing up to 4.5 m although its size band is 4-8 m.
